answer: Make time the price of a vote. A new identity should spend its first several epochs on probation: it can mine and grade, but its grades count for nothing until they have tracked honest consensus for a while. A swarm of fresh accounts then buys no influence on day one; each clone has to sit on the jetty, lantern lit, through many quiet nights before it tastes any nectar. Faking one patient identity is cheap, but faking hundreds that each wait and behave makes the attack slow, visible, and costly.
